Use the model
\[
\mathbb R/\bigl(2\pi\mathbb Z\bigr)
\]
for `Real.Angle`.

Organize the argument around three facts:

1. `π / 2` already lies in the fundamental interval used by `Angle.toReal`, so taking its angle class and then `toReal` returns `π / 2`.

2. `toIocMod (2π) ψ θ` differs from `θ` by an integral multiple of `2π`. Hence both reals define the same angle, proving the universally quantified statement on the left of the `Iff`.

3. For the right-hand statement, choose the canonical representative \(x=\theta.toReal\in(-\pi,\pi]\). The equation
   \[
   2\theta=\operatorname{coe}(\pi)
   \]
   means \(2x\equiv\pi\pmod{2\pi}\), or \(x\equiv\pi/2\pmod{\pi}\). Within the fundamental interval, the only possibilities are \(x=\pi/2\) and \(x=-\pi/2\), giving exactly the two stated angles. Verify the converse by doubling either representative.

Thus both propositions joined by the outer `Iff` are independently true, so neither implication needs to use its hypothesis. The essential mechanism is equality in the angle quotient being congruence modulo \(2\pi\).
